Quick reference

Course glossary

AND

Logical operator requiring every condition to be true.

AVG

Calculates the mean of non-NULL values.

Accidental cross join

Unintended multiplication caused by a missing condition.

Affected rows

Number of rows changed by a statement.

Aggregate function

A function that summarizes multiple rows.

Alias

A temporary name assigned in a query.

Alias requirement

A name assigned to the derived result.

Anchor member

Initial rows of a recursive query.

Anti join

Keeps base rows that have no match.

Atomicity

Property that all transaction steps succeed or none do.

Average order value

Revenue divided by qualifying orders.

BETWEEN

Tests an inclusive range.

Base population

The table whose rows must remain.

Benchmark

A reference value used for comparison.

Boundary

The lower or upper edge of a range.

Boundary value

Value at a defined start or end.

Bridge

An intermediate table connecting entities.

Business key

Fields that should uniquely identify a real-world record.

Business rule

Domain-specific validity requirement.

CASE

Conditional expression returning one value.

CAST

Explicitly converts a value to another type.

CHECK

Constraint testing an expression for inserted or updated rows.

COALESCE

Returns the first non-NULL expression.

COMMIT

Makes transaction changes permanent.

COUNT(*)

Counts rows, including rows containing NULL columns.

CROSS JOIN

Join returning the Cartesian product.

CTE

Named intermediate result defined with WITH.

Cardinality

The number of distinct values in a field.

Cartesian product

Every possible pair of rows.

Case sensitivity

Whether uppercase and lowercase are treated as different.

Cohort

Entities sharing a defined starting period or event.

Cohort month

Period of the first qualifying event.

Collation

Rules used to compare and order text.

Column

A named attribute with a data type.

Combination

The complete set of selected values considered for uniqueness.

Comment

Text ignored by the SQL engine and used for explanation.

Comparison operator

Symbol such as =, <>, >, or <= used to compare values.

Compatible columns

Columns aligned by count, position, and type.

Compatible grain

Numerator and denominator measured over the same population.

Completeness

Extent to which required values are present.

Concatenation

Combining text values.

Condition

A logical test used by a clause.

Conditional aggregation

Aggregate calculations restricted by a condition.

Conformed dimension

Shared dimension used consistently across facts.

Constraint

Rule enforced by the database.

Contract

Expected columns and grain produced by a stage.

Control report

Output showing checks, failures, and status.

Control total

A trusted value used for comparison.

Conversion rate

Entities reaching a later stage divided by an earlier stage.

Correlated predicate

Condition that refers to the outer row.

Correlated subquery

Subquery referencing the current outer row.

Current row

Frame boundary ending at the current position.

Customer grain

One row per customer.

DDL

SQL statements defining database objects.

DENSE_RANK

Tie-aware rank without gaps.

DISTINCT

Removes duplicate output rows.

DML

Statements that insert, update, or delete data.

Data profile

A summary of data structure and quality.

Data type

A definition of the kind of value a column holds.

Database

An organized collection of related data.

Date function

A function that extracts or transforms date/time values.

Date grain

The time level used for analysis, such as day or month.

Deduplication rule

Documented logic for resolving repeated records.

Default value

Value returned when the requested offset does not exist.

Deliverable

File or output required for review.

Denominator

The population used to calculate a rate.

Derived column

A result calculated rather than stored.

Derived table

A subquery used as a row source.

Deterministic order

An order fully defined by one or more columns.

Dialect

A database system’s implementation of SQL.

Dimension

A descriptive field used to split a metric.

Dimension table

Table of descriptive attributes used for filtering and grouping.

Division by zero

An invalid calculation prevented with an explicit rule.

Domain

The observed set of values in a field.

Double counting

Counting the same event more than once.

Drill-down

Moving from a summary to a more detailed grain.

Drop-off

Loss between two funnel stages.

Duplicate

A repeated record or repeated selected combination.

Duplicate group

Rows sharing the expected key.

ELSE

Fallback result when no WHEN matches.

EXISTS

Predicate that tests whether a subquery returns a row.

EXISTS subquery

Subquery used only to test presence.

Encapsulation

Hiding lower-level complexity behind a stable interface.

Equal-value split

Tied values placed in different bands due to row counts.

Equality

A test that two values are the same.

Execution context

Values available while an expression is evaluated.

Execution plan

Steps selected by the database to run a query.

Expression

A calculation or value returned as a column.

FIRST_VALUE

Returns the first value in the window frame.

FROM

Clause that identifies source tables.

Fact table

Table of measurable events at a defined grain.

Fallback

A substitute used when preferred data is absent.

False duplicate

Similar rows that legitimately represent different events.

Fan-out

Row multiplication caused by one-to-many joins.

Filter

A rule that removes rows from the result.

Filter stage

The point at which rows or groups are removed.

Finding

Evidence-supported statement from analysis.

Flag

A derived value identifying a business condition.

Foreign key

A column that references a row in another table.

Frame sensitivity

Dependence of a result on frame boundaries.

Frequency

Number of qualifying events.

Full scan

Reading all rows of a table.

Funnel

Ordered stages toward an outcome.

GROUP BY

Clause that forms groups of equal key values.

Grain

The real-world meaning of one row.

Grain transition

Changing from one row meaning to another.

Group-relative comparison

Comparison with a benchmark inside the row’s group.

HAVING

Clause that filters grouped results.

Hierarchy

A parent-child organizational structure.

IN

Tests whether a value belongs to a list or subquery.

INNER JOIN

Join that keeps matched row pairs only.

IS NULL

Predicate used to identify NULL values.

Implicit conversion

Automatic conversion performed by the database.

Inclusive

Including the stated endpoints.

Incomplete period

A reporting period that has not yet ended.

Indentation

Visual spacing that exposes query structure.

Index

Structure that can accelerate data access.

Indicator

A 1/0 value representing whether a condition is met.

Inequality

A test that values differ or fall on different sides of a threshold.

Intermediate grain

The row meaning used before a final summary.

Join audit

Checks proving a join behaved as intended.

Join chain

A sequence of relationships across multiple tables.

Join condition

Predicate defining how rows pair.

KPI

A defined measure linked to an objective.

LAG

Returns a prior row’s value.

LAST_VALUE

Returns the last value in the window frame.

LEAD

Returns a later row’s value.

LEFT JOIN

Join preserving every left-side row.

LIKE

Operator for simple text pattern matching.

LIMIT

Maximum number of rows returned.

Lag

Delay introduced by averaging past periods.

Limitation

Condition restricting interpretation or use.

Logical order

Conceptual order in which query clauses are evaluated.

Maintainability

Ease of safely reviewing and changing logic.

Matched row

A row whose key finds a counterpart.

Materialized view

Stored query result refreshed separately in systems that support it.

Measure

A numeric value summarized by an aggregate.

Metric definition

Population, formula, time period, and units of a KPI.

Metric grain

The level at which a metric is summarized.

Module

A self-contained query stage with one purpose.

Moving average

Average over a rolling window.

Multi-dimensional group

A group defined by more than one field.

NOT

Logical operator that reverses a condition.

NOT NULL

Constraint requiring a value.

NTILE

Assigns ordered rows to numbered groups.

NULL

A marker for missing or unknown data.

NULL extension

NULL values added for unmatched right-side columns.

NULLIF

Returns NULL when two values are equal.

Naming convention

A consistent rule for object and alias names.

Net revenue

Revenue after a stated discount rule.

Not applicable

A business reason a value may intentionally be absent.

Numerator

The counted or summed events of interest.

OFFSET

Number of rows skipped before returning results.

OR

Logical operator requiring at least one condition to be true.

ORDER BY

Clause that defines result sorting.

OVER

Clause defining a window calculation.

Operator precedence

Rules determining calculation order.

Optional match

A relationship that may be absent.

Orphan record

Child row without a valid parent.

Outer aggregation

Summary applied after an inner calculation.

Outer filter

Filter applied after the rank is calculated.

Outer query

The query containing a subquery.

Output stage

The point at which selected expressions are returned.

PARTITION BY

Divides rows into independent windows.

Parent row

A record referenced by another row.

Partition

Independent group for ranking.

Period number

Elapsed periods since cohort start.

Period-over-period

Comparison with the previous reporting period.

Pipeline stage

A logical transformation step.

Population

The set of rows included in the analysis.

Portability

How easily SQL logic moves between systems.

Portfolio project

Evidence of an end-to-end analytical workflow.

Post-aggregation filter

A HAVING condition applied after grouping.

PostgreSQL

The primary teaching dialect for production-style SQL.

Pre-aggregation filter

A WHERE condition applied before grouping.

Precedence

Rules controlling which condition is evaluated first.

Predicate

A condition that evaluates to true, false, or unknown.

Prefix search

Pattern matching from the start of text.

Presence test

Question of whether any related row exists.

Primary key

A column or set of columns that uniquely identifies a row.

Projection

Choosing the columns included in a result.

Quality audit

Repeatable set of tests for data fitness.

Quantile band

A segment based on relative position.

Quartile

One of four ordered groups.

Query

A statement sent to a database.

RANK

Tie-aware rank with gaps.

ROLLBACK

Cancels uncommitted changes.

ROW_NUMBER

Unique sequential row position.

Rate

A ratio representing frequency or proportion.

Ratio

One quantity divided by another.

Read-only role

Database permission that prevents modifications.

Readability

Ease with which query intent can be reviewed.

Recency

Time since the most recent qualifying event.

Reconciliation

Comparison of calculated values with trusted controls.

Reconciliation rule

Check that validates the final metric.

Recursive CTE

CTE that references itself.

Recursive member

Part that produces the next level.

Referential integrity

Requirement that references point to valid rows.

Relationship

A defined connection between table records.

Result grain

The meaning of one row in the grouped output.

Result set

Rows and columns returned by a query.

Retention

Continued qualifying activity after the start.

Rewrite

An alternative formulation using joins or windows.

Row

One record at the table grain.

Row multiplication

Increase caused by one-to-many matches.

Row source

Tables or derived tables available to a query.

Running total

Cumulative sum through the current row.

SELECT

Clause that defines returned columns or expressions.

SELECT 1

Convention showing returned subquery columns are irrelevant.

SQL

Structured Query Language used to work with relational data.

SQLite

The embedded engine used in the browser practice environment.

Sandbox

Isolated environment used for safe practice.

Scalar subquery

Subquery that returns one value.

Scenario grid

A complete set of combinations for planning or comparison.

Schema

The structural definition of database objects.

Scorecard

Compact set of monitored metrics.

Selectivity

How narrowly a condition reduces rows.

Self join

A join from a table to another instance of itself.

Semantic layer

Shared business definitions presented for analysis.

Semi join

Keeps base rows that have a match.

Set operation

Combines complete query results.

Short-circuit

Stopping after the first qualifying row.

Single-row requirement

Rule that scalar subqueries return at most one row.

Smoothing

Reducing short-term variation.

Stage

A defined event in the journey.

Standardization

Applying a consistent representation to values.

Star schema

Model with a central fact connected to dimensions.

String

Text data stored as characters.

TRIM

Removes leading and trailing spaces.

Table

A named set of rows with defined columns.

Table alias

A distinct name for each table instance.

Termination

Condition that stops recursion.

Threshold

A defined minimum or maximum rule.

Tie breaker

Additional sort key producing deterministic order.

Tie rule

Defined treatment of equal values.

Time zone

A regional rule for interpreting timestamps.

Top N per group

Highest-ranked rows retained inside every partition.

Transaction

A unit of work committed or rolled back together.

Type mismatch

A conflict between incompatible value types.

UNBOUNDED PRECEDING

Frame boundary starting at the first row.

UNION

Stacks results and removes duplicates.

UNION ALL

Stacks results and preserves duplicates.

Uniqueness

Extent to which expected keys are not duplicated.

Unknown

The third logical state produced by some NULL comparisons.

Unmatched row

A row without a qualifying counterpart.

Unmatched-key report

A list of keys failing to join.

Validation checkpoint

A count or total checked after each transformation.

Validation query

Check that confirms a stage behaved correctly.

Validity

Extent to which values follow allowed rules.

Value band

Relative segment based on customer value.

View

Named stored query exposed as a virtual table.

WHEN

A condition branch inside CASE.

WITH clause

Clause that introduces one or more CTEs.

Wide dataset

A result containing columns from several sources.

Wildcard

A symbol representing unknown characters.

Window frame

Subset of window rows available to a function.

Window function

Function evaluated over related rows without collapsing them.

Window order

Order used inside a window calculation.

Window size

Number of rows or periods included.
